Hi John — thanks for the clear questions. High level answers below, plus attached term sheet and activation checklist. Happy to jump on a call if you'd like to walk through.

Summary answers:
- Buyer eligibility: Private offers are issued to an AWS payer account. That payer can act on behalf of linked accounts (subsidiaries) — you should confirm the linked account configuration in your AWS Org. We typically require the buyer to be the payer account or an authorized purchaser listed on the offer.
- Term lengths: Standard options are 12, 24, or 36 months. We can provide deeper list-price discounts for 24+ month commitments or higher committed spend. Example pricing options attached (MPO_Pricing_Options.csv).
- Internal approvals: For Acme-like deals we advise: procurement + procurement director signoff, CFO signoff for one-time credits or discounts > $250k ARR impact, and legal review for multi-year deviations (early termination, data residency clauses).
- Activation lead time: Once private offer is accepted in AWS, activation is typically 24-72 hours for hosted customers; full onboarding (SAML, VPC/private deployments) can take 1-3 weeks depending on technical onboarding needs.

Thanks for the context — quick notes on approvals and best playbook: 

- Discount authority: Sales can approve up to 20% list discount on MPOs for standard terms. Anything >20% or that includes multi-year price-locks >24 months requires finance (Karthik) and legal review.
- One-time credits: Up to 12% of first-year ARR can be approved by sales for pilot/onboarding credits; >12% needs finance approval.
- Terming: Recommend pitching 24 months with an optional 12-month early-exit with pro-rated refund language (this reduces legal friction). For strategic logos with cross-subsidiary footprint, 36 months is an option if finance signs off on the discount depth.
- Buyer onboarding gating: Ensure Acme's payer account is enrolled in Marketplace (we can share enrollment steps). Also confirm the AWS account email matches the buyer identity on the PO — AWS will reject mismatched payer info.

Operational asks for the thread response:
1) Vivek — propose a concrete pricing example in the next reply (list price, discount %, credit amount, estimated activation ETA).
2) If we need >20% discount or >12% credit, loop Karthik for approval and prepare an abbreviated business case (ARR, logo value, renewal probability).
